data.title: China leaves lending benchmarks unchanged for 18th straight month in November
data.description:
China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged on Friday for the 18th straight month in November, in line with market expectations.

WHY IT'S IMPORTANT

The steady loan prime rates (LPRs) suggest lenders' net interest margins (NIMs) remain under pressure, offering little incentive for them to lower borrowing costs, even as the central bank has shifted its primary policy anchor to an overnight lending rate.

BY THE NUMBERS

The one-year loan prime rate (LPR) (CNYLPR1Y=CFXS) was kept at 3.00%, while the five-year LPR (CNYLPR5Y=CFXS) was unchanged at 3.50%.

In a Reuters survey of 28 market participants conducted this week, 23, or 82% of all respondents, predicted that both rates would remain steady.

The other five expected a cut to one or both rates.

CONTEXT

China's central bank formally shifted its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repo rate from the seven-day rate this month, a move analysts said ​would ease funding conditions and support the economy.

The change effectively lowered the floor of the interest-rate framework by 15 basis points, reducing borrowing costs ​for financial institutions.

The PBOC said it would shift the loan pricing benchmark from relying primarily on the LPR toward more diversified benchmarks, highlighting the overnight rate as an additional pricing reference.

China's economy showed fresh signs of sluggishness in October as factory production slowed and consumption remained weak, calling ​into question how long it can rely on exports to underpin growth.

KEY QUOTES

** Selena Ling, chief economist at OCBC

"The new overnight policy rate of 1.25% is below the previous seven-day benchmark of 1.40%, helping guide short-term funding costs lower. Against this backdrop, we see less urgency for an immediate reduction in the LPR and expect only a 10-basis-point LPR cut in 2027, primarily to ease funding pressures on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)."

data.title: Japan Tobacco Shares Slump After $8.6 Billion Hit From Russia Business
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

Japan Tobacco shares fell sharply early Friday after the company projected an $8.6 billion hit stemming from the loss of control over its Russian operations.

Shares recently traded 9.0% lower at 5,329 yen, equivalent to $33.37, in Tokyo.

The Japanese tobacco maker said late Thursday that it would book a loss of 1.377 trillion yen, equivalent to $8.62 billion, as a result of losing control of the Russian business.

Earlier this month, Japan Tobacco reported that all seven of its Russian entities were placed under temporary administration by a Russian company under orders from President Vladimir Putin.

Japan Tobacco projected a net loss of Y724.00 billion for 2026, reversing its previous net-profit view owing primarily to the special loss related to the Russian business. The company also cut its dividend forecast for this year to Y204 a share from Y272.

The tobacco maker said it remained confident it could raise dividends in the coming years, supported by profit growth.

Japan Tobacco had expected Russia to account for about 10% of its revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit in 2026.

The tobacco maker has the ability to generate strong profit and cash flow in markets other than Russia, but its creditworthiness could be weighed by a big loss and lower profitability due to the removal of the Russian business from consolidated reporting, said Yasuaki Kudamatsu, senior credit analyst at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities.

Write to Kosaku Narioka at kosaku.narioka@wsj.com

data.title: CVR Energy Announces Pricing of $1.25 Billion of 9.250% Senior Secured Notes Due 2032
data.description:
CVR Energy, Inc. (the “Company” or “CVR Energy”) () announced today the pricing of its previously announced private placement (the “Offering”) pursuant to Rule 144A and Regulation S under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), of $1.25 billion in aggregate principal amount of 9.250% senior secured notes due 2032 (the “Notes”). The Notes will be issued at a price equal to 98.980% of their principal amount. The Notes will mature on March 15, 2032. The Offering is expected to close on November 25, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Prior to the closing of the Acquisition (as defined below), the Notes will not be guaranteed and will be secured only by a first-priority security interest in favor of the trustee in the Company’s rights to an escrow account and the funds held therein. Upon the closing of the Acquisition, the Notes are expected to be fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior secured basis by each of the Company’s existing and future wholly-owned domestic restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the Company’s new senior secured credit facilities or certain of its other material indebtedness.

In addition, the Company is seeking to enter into a new senior secured term loan B facility in an aggregate principal amount of $1.0 billion and to amend its existing senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility to increase aggregate commitments from $550 million to $1.1 billion. These financing transactions are expected to close substantially concurrently with the Acquisition and are subject to market and other conditions.

Upon the closing of the Acquisition, the Notes and related guarantees are expected to be secured by (i) first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors other than excluded assets and assets securing the Company’s asset-based revolving credit facility on a first-priority basis (the “ABL Priority Collateral”) and (ii) second-priority liens on the ABL Priority Collateral, in each case subject to permitted liens and exceptions.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering, together with cash on hand and the net proceeds from other related financing transactions, to fund the previously announced acquisition of the St. Paul Park, Minnesota and Mandan, North Dakota refineries and related marketing business from certain subsidiaries of Marathon Petroleum Corporation and MPLX LP (the “Acquisition”), redeem the Company’s outstanding 5.750% Senior Notes due 2028 (the “2028 Notes”) and pay related fees and expenses.

The Offering is not conditioned on the consummation of the Acquisition or the other financing transactions. The net proceeds from the Offering are expected to be deposited into an escrow account pending satisfaction of specified release conditions. If the Acquisition is not consummated on or before October 28, 2027, or the purchase agreement governing the Acquisition is terminated in accordance with its terms, the Company will be required to redeem the Notes at a redemption price equal to 100% of their issue price, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the redemption date.

The offer and sale of the Notes and the related guarantees have not been registered under the Securities Act, or any state securities laws, and unless so registered, these securities may not be offered or sold in the United States except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws. The Company plans to offer and sell these securities only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act and to non-U.S. persons outside the United States pursuant to Regulation S under the Securities Act.

This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, any of these securities or any other securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities or any other securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. This news release shall not constitute a notice of redemption under the indenture governing the 2028 Notes.

data.title: Asian Equities Fall as Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Fails to Staunch AI Stock Selloff
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities fell Friday morning as Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering failed to staunch the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks.

"The central story was the paradox of a record-breaking AI-sector IPO failing to arrest a broader market selloff," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report. "Rather than acting as a rising tide, the listing appeared to trigger rotation out of existing AI-related names as investors redeployed capital into the new issue," they said.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in the largest IPO on record, ending the overnight session with a market capitalization of roughly $1.3 trillion.

Anthropic shares opened more than 30% above their $83 IPO price, though gains moderated during the session to finish up 17% at $97.17 in their market debut. The pullback "coincided with declines in other AI-related stocks amid concerns about how higher interest rates affect technology valuations," said Antonio Di Giacomo, senior market analyst at XS.com, in an email.

The SPDR Select Sector Technology exchange-traded fund, which tracks the tech industry group of the U.S.' S&P 500, entered bear-market territory on Thursday, closing 1.9% lower at $160.69, more than 20% below its October peak.

Across Asia, South Korea's Kospi slid 4.7%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix shedding 6.3% and Samsung Electronics losing 4.8%. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average slipped 4.7%, as AI proxy SoftBank Group fell 15.6%, memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings dropped 12.6%, and Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic test equipment for the semiconductor industry, declined 12.3%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 benchmark index was down 0.9%.

Short-dated Asian and U.S. government bonds rose in price terms Friday morning as the equity-markets' selloff bolstered safe-haven demand for sovereign debt.

Yields on Australia's two-year government bonds declined 4 basis points to 4.6150% and on New Zealand's two-year sovereign notes fell 2 basis points to 3.8740%. U.S. two-year Treasury yields edged 2 basis points lower to 4.7429%% following Thursday's Treasury yield declines. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

"Risk aversion intensified, driving demand for U.S. Treasurys," two strategists at OCBC Group Research said in a report. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks," the strategists added.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

data.title: China Stock Market Tipped To Open Under Water On Friday
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - The China stock market turned lower again on Thursday, one day after ending the four-day losing streak in which it had slumped almost 100 points or 2.7 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,580-point plateau and the losses may accelerate on Friday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is weak on continuing AI concerns and rising crude oil prices. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourses are expected to open in similar fashion.

The SCI finished modestly lower on Thursday as losses from the retail, technology, industrial and transportation stocks were offset by gains from the financials and communications companies.

For the day, the index slipped 10.21 points or 0.28 percent to finish at 3,577.62 after trading between 3,547.94 and 3,584.28. The Shenzhen Composite Index dropped 29.71 points or 1.47 percent to end at 1,997.54.

The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as the major averages opened slightly higher on Thursday but quickly turned lower and continued to accelerate to the downside throughout the session, ending at daily lows.

The Dow plunged 1,101.11 points or 2.19 percent to finish at 49,097.06, while the NASDAQ tumbled 550.69 points or 2.25 percent to close at 23,879.20 and the S&P 500 crashed 147.80 points or 2.02 percent to end at 7,175.83.

The markets initially benefited from a positive reaction to artificial intelligence company Anthropic's (ANT) initial public offering. Buying interest waned shortly after the start of trading, however, and selling pressure intensified soon after intelligence company Anthropic made its debut on the NASDAQ.

While the Claude developer priced its initial public offering at a higher-than-expected $83 per share and soared by nearly 40 percent as it began trading, the stock pulled back well off its highs as the day progressed. The pullback by Anthropic and the sell-off was attributed to profit taking amid lingering concerns about where the AI trade goes from here.

In U.S. economic news, the Labor Department released a report showing first-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits unexpectedly edged higher last week.

Crude oil prices edged higher on Thursday as fears of supply disruptions increased in the Strait of Hormuz. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was up $0.17 or 0.20 percent at $83.43 per barrel.
